text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA

- Fifteenth day of demonstrations in Belgrade over annulment of local elections rallies 70,000. "We will greet the New Year in Terazije," members of opposition coalition Zajedno announce. Protests continue in other towns in Serbia.
- Federal Ministry for Transport and Communications bans independent Radio B-92 broadcasts because it did not have a permit.
- Twelfth day of student protests in Belgrade rallies more than 20,000.
- Montenegrin opposition protests outside Montenegro TV in Podgorica in support of Serbian opposition and against media blockade of events in Serbia.
- Association of Independent Journalists of Serbia calls for Serbian Information Minister Aleksandar Tijanic's resignation over closure of independent Radio B-92.

- Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Serbia says Serbian parliament president Dragan Tomic overstepped his powers and abused his position when he described "legitimate protests of citizens as fascist demonstrations".
- Independent trade union Nezavisnost calls workers to general strike over election fraud.
- Protection of "socially-owned" property against privatisation will lead to destruction of social capital, says economist Veselin Vukotic.
- Federal government to decide on wheat imports Thursday.
POLITIKA
- Serbian government discusses amendments to draft laws on labour, employment and pension and disablement insurance. The laws are on the agenda of the next parliament session.
- Yugoslav Army Chief of General Staff General Momcilo Perisic in Romania for talks on Yugoslav-Romanian military cooperation.
- Serbia's projected 1997 GDP growth 13 percent, exports 37 percent.
- Without radical economic reforms it will be difficult to achieve the great expectations of next year, economists agree at seminar of economists of Yugoslavia.
- Fourth round of local elections at 16 polling stations in Belgrade on Saturday, December 7.
- Coalition Zajedno rally paralyses traffic in central Belgrade for hours.
- Bosnian Serb prime minister Gojko Klickovic says a protectorate of any kind for the disputed town of Brcko is out of question.
BORBA
- First session of new federal parliamentary chamber of citizens on scheduled for December 10.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- "We cannot divide only what is on the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, but what was on the entire territory of the former Yugoslavia," says Vladan Kutlesic, member of Yugoslav team negotiating in succession talks.
